reuse.why: The two link rules are shared helpers used by every provider, but the Fintegra link and download functions are fresh copies of existing provider code and the takeover path re-writes unlinkAccount's field clearing instead of reusing it.

duplication.why: linkFintegraAccount is a sixth copy of the link body, downloadFintegraTransactions copies the Enable Banking download, the unlink field-clearing block is copied from unlinkAccount, and six near-identical registration wrappers repeat the same guard sequence.

placement.why: Guards live in app.ts next to the link handlers, but they are bolted on as inline lambdas in the app.method registrations rather than inside the link flow, and a function named ensure... silently mutates another account.

scope.why: Changes are confined to the linking flow, the new provider plumbing and a focused test file.

maintainability.why: Every future provider must remember to copy both the link body and the wrapper with the right provider string, and the takeover unlink can drift from unlinkAccount.

bypasses_abstraction.where: ensureBankAccountIsNotLinked clears the old link with its own db.updateAccount instead of going through unlinkAccount (e.g. with an option to skip the provider-side cleanup).

disguised_duplication.where: The copies (linkFintegraAccount, downloadFintegraTransactions, the unlink field list, the six wrappers) are verbatim or near-verbatim, not disguised.

abstraction_drift.where: ensureBankAccountIsNotLinked gains the replaceExistingLink parameter and a branch that performs the unlink inside a check helper; that branch bypasses unlinkAccount.
